article_content: The people of Gaza have given the Palestinian struggle a new impetus and direction. It is Gaza again, but this time it is different! Instead of reacting to apartheid Israel’s regular genocidal attacks, the resistance movements have taken the initiative in an unprecedented move. Rather than waiting for Israel’s 'generosity' to open one of the seven gates of the world’s largest open-air prison, the inmates—inspired by the Warsaw Uprising of 1944—decided to take matters into their own hands. The deadly medieval siege imposed on Gaza since 2007, supported by the European Union and the United States, along with recurrent genocidal wars launched by Israel, aims to make the Palestinians of Gaza disappear slowly and painfully. No more! Enough is enough. The resistance movements in Gaza, both right and left, have decided to turn the tables. They have given the Palestinian struggle a new impetus and a clear direction towards liberation and decolonization. To understand today’s events, it is important to remember the context of the Palestinian struggle over the past 30 years. The decision by the Palestinian Liberation Organisation (PLO) leadership to coexist with Zionism led to the disastrous Oslo Accords, which effectively truncated Palestinian history. The Naksa—the Israeli occupation of the West Bank, Gaza, the Golan Heights, and the Sinai desert in 1967—became separate from the Nakba—the mass expulsion of Palestinians from their homeland in 1948. The focus shifted to the occupation rather than the settler colonialism behind it, while 'peace negotiations' served as a cover for Israeli violence and continued dispossession of the Palestinians. As Israeli historian Ilan Pappe maintains in his book 'The Biggest Prison on Earth': 'Israeli strategists discovered that if you want to implement ethnic cleansing by other means, the alternative to expulsion is not to allow people to leave the place where they live—and thus they can be excluded from the democratic balance of power. They are contained inside their own areas but do not have to be counted in the overall national demographics since they cannot freely move, develop, or expand, nor do they have any basic civil and human rights.' Apartheid Israel has made it clear that since it cannot eliminate us completely, we must become its slaves, people without any rights. The majority of Israeli Jews support the genocidal policy of their governments because, as Zionists living in apartheid Israel, they are indoctrinated into believing that they are entitled to certain privileges that must be denied to the indigenous population of the land. In 1948, ethnic cleansing was the solution. In 1967, enslavement became the only option. In the face of this reality, Palestinians have reached common ground on the enemy being settler colonialism, but they have failed to agree on how decolonization should be understood and achieved. In recent years, there has been a radical shift in strategic thinking, viewing Israeli-Palestinian relations within the framework of settler colonialism and apartheid. True liberation within this context means achieving true equality in historic Palestine after the return of all Palestinian refugees to the towns and villages from which they were ethnically cleansed in 1948. No wonder Gaza has decided to take this unprecedented move. Two-thirds of Gazans are refugees entitled to their right of return in accordance with United Nations General Assembly Resolution 194 of 1948. It is rumored that the resistance fighters who managed to enter Sderot are the grandsons of refugees from the village of Huj, which was ethnically cleansed by Zionist militias in 1948 and renamed Sderot. Others are from the village of Hirbya, renamed Zikim by the Israelis. They have dared to do the 'unthinkable'—return, not as visitors granted permission by the colonizer, but as liberators upholding their right to their ancestral land. This radical act of return points to the post-Zionist future we should envision that will bring liberation to all. Liberation for us means dismantling the structures of Zionist settler colonialism and apartheid and addressing the inequalities and injustices it has inflicted on us, the indigenous population of Palestine, over the past 100 years. Liberation for us aims to transform the relationship between Palestinians and Israelis into one based on total equality and justice. The settler society is expected to abandon all colonial privileges and display real willingness to accept responsibility for past crimes and injustices. The compromise that indigenous Palestinians are expected to offer is to accept settlers as equal citizens in the new state between the Jordan River and the Mediterranean Sea. This is the path to peace and security, and the international community, which has long accepted Israel’s war crimes against the Palestinians and has even been complicit in them, will have to embrace it. Having learned nothing from history, US President Joe Biden made it clear the day Palestinian fighters crossed through the barbed wire to Israel that he is fully behind Israel, giving its army the green light to commit more war crimes against the civilians of Gaza. Three days after the start of the resistance inside 1948 Palestine, Israel has killed more than 770 people in Gaza, including 140 children, and injured 4,000. More than 180,000 people have had to flee their homes as their neighborhoods have been viciously targeted by Israeli warplanes; I am one of them. Leaders like Biden would do well to remember Brazilian educator and philosopher Paulo Freire’s words: 'With the establishment of a relationship of oppression, violence has already begun. Never in history has violence been initiated by the oppressed. How could they be the initiators if they themselves are the result of violence? … There would be no oppressed had there been no prior situation of violence to establish their subjugation. Violence is initiated by those who oppress, who exploit, who fail to recognize others as people—not by those who are oppressed, exploited, and unrecognized.' In Gaza and Jenin, we refuse to march to Israel’s death chambers like sheep. In Gaza and Jenin—in fact, in all of historic Palestine—we have made it absolutely clear that we will resist the settler, colonial, apartheid regime between the Jordan River and the Mediterranean. And we expect the international community to support our struggle for justice and freedom in exactly the same way as it has supported the Ukrainian resistance against the Russian invasion. The double standards we have seen have convinced us that it is our duty as Palestinians to create the political space for our liberation where none has been afforded to us. We cannot compromise on our basic rights, including the right to self-determination and the right of return. We have a clear path towards liberation that strays away from the facade of talking independence and camouflaged racist solutions. translated_content: Gazos gyventojai suteikė palestiniečių kovai naują impulsą ir kryptį. Tai vėl Gaza, bet šįkart viskas yra kitaip! Viešpataujant izoliacijai, Izraelio apartheido reguliari genocido puolimai nebegali būti tik reakcija. Pasipriešinimo judėjimai ėmė pirmąjį žingsnį beprecedentiniame veiksme. Nors Izraelis nesuteikia 'malonės' atidaryti vienus iš septynių didžiausių pasaulio lauko kalėjimų vartų, kaliniai – įkvėpti 1944 m. Varšuvos sukilimo – nusprendė imtis reikalų į savo rankas. Mirtina viduramžiška apsupty, įvesta Gazoje nuo 2007 m., remiama Europos Sąjungos ir Jungtinių Valstijų, kartu su Izraelio reguliariais genocido karais, siekia lėtai ir skausmingai išnaikinti Gazos palestiniečius. Daugiau! Užteko! Dešinieji ir kairieji pasipriešinimo judėjimai Gazoje nusprendė pertvarkyti žaidimą. Jie suteikė palestiniečių kovai naują impulsą ir aiškią kryptį link išsilaisvinimo ir dekolonizacijos. Norint suprasti šiandienos įvykius, svarbu prisiminti palestiniečių kovos kontekstą per pastarąjį 30 metų laikotarpį. Palestinos išsivadavimo organizacijos (PLO) vadovybės sprendimas gyventi kartu su sionizmu privedė prie katastrofiškų Oslos sutarčių, kurios faktiškai nutraukė palestiniečių istoriją. Naksa – Izraelio okupacija Vakarų Krante, Gazoje, Golanau ir Sinajaus dykumoje 1967 m. – tapo atskirta nuo Nakbos – palestiniečių masinio išvarymo iš jų gimtinės 1948 m. Dėmesys buvo sutelktas į okupaciją, o ne į kolonistinį kolonializmą, esantį už jo, o 'taikos derybos' tarnavo kaip Izraelio smurto ir palestiniečių tolesnio atimamojo dėviklio denglis. Kaip Izraelio istorikas Ilanas Papė teigia savo knygoje 'Didžiausias kalėjimas ant žemės': 'Izraelio strategai išsiaiškino, kad jei norite įgyvendinti etninį valymą kitais būdais, alternatyva išvarymui yra neleisti žmonėms palikti vietos, kurioje jie gyvena – ir taip jie gali būti pašalinti iš demokratinio jėgų balanso. Jie yra apriboti savo teritorijoje, bet jų nereikia skaičiuoti bendrojoje nacionalinėje demografijoje, nes jie negali laisvai judėti, vystytis ar plėstis, ir neturi jokių pagrindinių piliečių ir žmogaus teisių.' Apartheido Izraelis aiškiai parodė, kad nesugebėjęs mūsų visiškai sunaikinti, mes turime tapti jo vergais, žmonėmis be jokių teisių. Dauguma Izraelio žydų rėmė savo vyriausybės genocido politiką, nes kaip sionistai, gyvenantys apartheido Izraelyje, jie yra indoktrinuoti manyti, kad turi teisę į tam tikras privilegijas, kurios turi būti atmestos vietiniam gyventojams. 1948 m. etninis valymas buvo sprendimas. 1967 m. vergovė tapo vienintele galimybe. Šiame kontekste palestiniečiai susitarė dėl kolonistinio kolonializmo kaip priešo, bet nesutarė, kaip dekolonizacija turėtų būti suprasta ir įgyvendinta. Paskutiniuosiuose metuose įvyko radikalus strateginis mąstymo posūkis, kuris mato Izraelio-Palestinos santykius kolonistinio kolonializmo ir apartheido kontekte. Tikroji išsilaisvinimas šiame kontekste reiškia pasiekti tikrą lygybę istorinėje Palestinoje po visų palestiniečių pabėgėlių grįžimo į miestus ir kaimus, iš kurių jie buvo etniškai išvalyti 1948 m. Nenuostabu, kad Gaza nusprendė įvykdyti šį beprecedentį žingsnį. Dvi trečdalys Gazos gyventojų yra pabėgėliai, turintys teisę grįžti pagal Jungtinių Tautų Generalinės Asamblėjos 1948 m. rezoliuciją Nr. 194. Girdimasi, kad pasipriešinimo kovotojai, pavyko patekti į Sderotą, yra 1948 m. sionistų milicijos etniškai išvalyto Huj kaimo pabėgėlių anūkai, pervadintas Sderotu. Kitų pabėgėlių protėviai yra iš Hirbya kaimo, pervadinto Zikim. Jie išdrįso padaryti 'neįsivaizduojamą' – grįžti ne kaip lankytojai, turintys kolonizatoriaus leidimą, bet kaip išvaduotojai, ginantys savo teisę į savo protėvių žemę. Šis radikalus grįžimo aktas rodo post-sionistinę ateitį, kurią turime įsivaizduoti ir kuri atneš išsilaisvinimą visiems. Mūsų išsilaisvinimas reiškia nugriauti Zionistinio kolonistinio kolonializmo ir apartheido struktūras ir išspręsti nelygybes ir neteisingumus, kurie mums buvo padaryti per pastarąjį šimtmetį. Mūsų išsilaisvinimas siekia transformuoti santykius tarp palestiniečių ir izraeliečių į pilnai lygias ir teisingas. Kolonistinė visuomenė turi atsisakyti visų kolonijinių privilegijų ir parodyti tikrą norą pripažinti atsakomybę už praeities nusikaltimus ir neteisingumus. Indėnų palestiniečiai turi pasiūlyti kompromisą – pripažinti naujoje valstybėje tarp Jordano upės ir Viduržemio jūros kolonus kaip lygiavertius piliečius. Tai yra kelias į taiką ir saugumą, ir tarptautinė bendruomenė, kuri ilgai pripažino Izraelio karinius nusikaltimus prieš palestiniečius ir net buvo juose įsipainiojusi, turės jį pripažinti. Nemokydami iš istorijos, JAV prezidentas Džo Baidenas aiškiai parodė dieną, kai palestiniečių kovotojai peržengė spygliuotą vielą į Izraelį, kad jis visiškai remia Izraelį, suteikdamas jo armijai žalią šviesą daryti dar daugiau karinių nusikaltimų prieš Gazos gyventojus. Praėjus trejiems dienoms po pasipriešinimo pradžios 1948 m. Palestinoje, Izraelis nužudė daugiau kaip 770 žmonių Gazzoje, įskaitant 140 vaikų, ir sužeidė 4000. Daugiau kaip 180 000 žmonių turėjo palikti savo namus, kai jų kvartalai buvo žiauriai apšaudomi Izraelio lėktuvais; aš esu vienas iš jų. Lyderiai, tokie kaip Baidenas, turėtų gerai prisiminti Brazilijos švietėjo ir filosofo Paulo Freire žodžius: 'Su įkūrimu priespaudos santykių, smurtas jau prasidėjo. Istorijoje niekada smurtas nebuvo pradėtas nuo priespaudos. Kaip jie galėtų būti pradėjėjai, jei jie patys yra priespaudos rezultatas? … Nebūtų priespaudos, jei nebūtų ankstesnės smurto situacijos, nustatančios jų pavaldumą. Smurtas yra pradedamas tuo, kurie spaudžia, eksploatuoja, kurie nesugeba pripažinti kitų kaip žmonių – ne tuo, kurie yra priespaudos, eksploatuojami ir nepripažįstami.' Gazoje ir Dženine mes atsisakome eiti į Izraelio mirties kameras kaip avys. Gazoje ir Dženine – faktiškai, visoje istorinėje Palestinoje – mes aiškiai parodėme, kad pasipriešinsime kolonistiniam, kolonialiniam, apartheido režimui tarp Jordano upės ir Viduržemio jūros. Ir mes tikimės, kad tarptautinė bendruomenė parėms mūsų kovą dėl teisingumo ir laisvės tiek pat, kiek ji parėmė ukrainiečių pasipriešinimą prieš Rusijos invaziją. Dvigubi standartai, kuriuos mes matėme, įkalbė mus, palestiniečius, kad mūsų pareiga yra sukurti politinę erdvę mūsų išsilaisvinimui, kurio niekas mums nesuteikė. Mes negalime apsiriboti esminiais teisėmis, įskaitant savivaldos ir grįžimo teisę. Turime aiškią kelią link išsilaisvinimo, nukrypstančią nuo nepriklausomybės šnekėjimo fasado ir maskuotų rasistinių sprendimų. Šiame straipsnyje išreikštos nuomonės yra autoriaus asmeninės ir nebūtinai atspindi Al Jazeera redakcinę poziciją.

article_content: Bath made a sensational comeback in their Champions Cup campaign yesterday, showcasing a vision of midfield brilliance that England could benefit from. This victory over one of Europe's top teams ranks among the finest achievements by Premiership sides in continental competitions. Toulouse, having lost only one of their last 17 home matches against English opposition, were overwhelmed by Mike Ford's relentless team. The bonus-point win significantly boosts Bath's chances of reaching the quarter-finals. Ross Barry (second left) signals to his teammates during Bath's triumph over Toulouse. If Bath secures a home win against Glasgow and scores four tries, Toulouse would need a perfect outcome in their match against Montpellier to top the pool. Even if Bath misses the top spot, they could still advance as one of the top three runners-up. However, these strategic considerations were not the focus in the away dressing room last night. This stand-alone performance was remarkable in both quality and scale. Bath won with confidence and style, seizing every opportunity to attack with breathtaking cohesion and intent. In the first half, their play was exceptional, nearly securing the win before halftime. The England trio of George Ford, Kyle Eastmond, and Jonathan Joseph were particularly impressive, tearing through Toulouse's defense. Joseph's late bonus-point try, created by a chip and a brilliant run, was a highlight. This collective display of skill will give England's coaches much to consider as they finalize their Six Nations squad. Ford is a sure pick at fly-half, but there is growing demand for Eastmond and Joseph to join him. Mike Ford, Bath's director of rugby, praised his players after the epic win at Stade Ernest Wallon, describing Joseph's performance as 'sublime, outstanding, world class.' He noted that Joseph is close to a Test return, depending on England's playing style. If England's coaches want to utilize their wide runners, the first half of this match should convince them to include Eastmond and Joseph. Their inspired play stunned the stadium. An early penalty by George Ford was followed by a swift try in the seventh minute. Leroy Houston's drive and Chris Cook's off-load set up Francois Louw to send Matt Banahan scoring. Ford's conversion gave Bath a commanding lead. Toulouse briefly fought back with a try from a lineout drive, but Bath quickly regained control. In the 24th minute, Cook intercepted a pass and scored an 80-meter try. Moments later, Eastmond broke free, passed to Banahan, who then set up Joseph for another try. Bath nearly sealed the win with a raid led by Horacio Agulla, Ford, and Joseph, but Anthony Watson missed the chance. Despite Yoann Huget's try for Toulouse, Bath's resilience and flair secured the victory. George Ford's tackle on Yannick Nyanga and crucial scrum penalties were turning points. A double-team tackle by Matt Garvey and Carl Fearns exemplified Bath's defense. Joseph's creative try nine minutes from the end, involving a chip kick and a swerving run, capped a magnificent performance. This win suggests Bath is poised to return to Europe's top tier after a long absence.

Jei Bath'as laimės namuose prieš Glazgą ir pelnys keturis įvarčius, Tulūzai reikės idealaus rezultato savo susitikime su Monpeljė, norint užimti pirmąją vietą grupėje. Pirmame kėlinyje jų žaidimas buvo išskirtinis, beveik užsitikrindamas pergalę dar iki pertraukos. Anglijos trijulė George Ford, Kyle Eastmond ir Jonathan Joseph buvo ypač įspūdingi, ardydami Tulūzos gynybą. Joseph'o vėlyvasis taškų įvarčio pelnytas smūgiu ir puikiu bėgimu buvo vienas iš ryškiausių momentų. Šis kolektyvinis meistriškumo parodymas duos Anglijos treneriams daug ko apmąstyti, renkantis Šešių Nacijų čempionato sudėtį. Fordas yra tikras pasirinkimas į atkirąjį pusę, bet vis didesnis reikalavimas, kad Eastmond ir Joseph prisijungtų prie jo. Mike Fordas, Bath'o regbio direktorius, gyrė savo žaidėjus po epinės pergalės Stade Ernest Wallon stadione, apibūdindamas Joseph'o pasirodymą kaip 'puikų, išskirtinį, pasaulio klasės'. Jis pažymėjo, kad Josephas yra arti grįžimo į Test rinktinę, priklausomai nuo Anglijos žaidimo stiliaus. Jei Anglijos treneriai nori išnaudoti savo plačiųjų bėgikų potencialą, pirmasis pusmėtis šiose varžybose turėtų juos įtikinti įtraukti Eastmondą ir Josephą. Jų įkvėptas žaidimas sužavėjo stadioną. Ankstyvasis George'o Fordo baudos smūgis buvo sekęs greitas įvarčio pelnytas septintąją minutę. Leroy Houston'o smūgis ir Chris Cook'o perdavimas leido Francois Louwui nukreipti milžinišką sparną Matt Banahanui. Fordo konversija suteikė Bath'ui vyraujančią poziciją. Tulūza trumpam atsakė įvarčiu iš autų, bet Bath'as greitai atgavo kontrolę. 24-ąją minutę Cookas perėmė perdavimą ir pelnė 80 metrų įvartį. Po kelių minučių Eastmondas išsiveržė, perdavė Banahanui, kuris savo ruožtu paruošė Josephui pelnyti kitą įvartį. Bath'as beveik užsitikrino pergalę su Horacio Agulla, Fordo ir Joseph'o vadovaujama puolima, bet Anthony Watsonas praleido progą. Nors Yoann Hugetas pelnė įvartį Tulūzos naudai, Bath'o atsparumas ir žavingumas užsitikrino pergalę. George'o Fordo atakavimas į Yannick Nyanga ir svarbios kovos baudos buvo posūkio taškai. Matt Garvey ir Carl Fearns duobulinė ataka buvo Bath'o gynybos pavyzdys. Joseph'o kūrybinis įvarčio pelnytas devintąją minutę iki pabaigos, įtraukiant smūgį ir lenkimą, užbaigė puikią pasirodymą. Ši pergalė rodo, kad Bath'as yra pasiruošęs grįžti į Europos elitą po ilgos pertraukos.

article_content: Enjoying a few glasses of wine after work might be more harmful than beneficial, according to recent research from the University of Sydney. While numerous past studies suggested that moderate alcohol consumption could protect against heart disease, this new study challenges that notion. The research, titled 'Alcohol’s Evaporating Health Benefits', examined the link between alcohol intake and mortality across various age groups, aiming to establish suitable age-specific alcohol limits and better define 'non-drinkers'. One of the study’s authors, Associate Professor Emmanuel Stamatakis from the University of Sydney’s Faculty of Health Sciences and Charles Perkins Centre, noted that prior research often exaggerated the benefits of daily moderate drinking. He explained that these studies were skewed by including non-drinkers without considering their reasons for abstinence, such as health issues or personal choices. In their new approach, the researchers first compared moderate drinkers with ex-drinkers and found protective benefits across all age groups. However, when they separated never-drinkers as a distinct group, these benefits vanished. 'Previous studies included non-drinkers without differentiating why they don’t drink. This group can include those who never drank, those who stopped due to health advice, or those with drinking problems,' said Assoc Prof Stamatakis. 'Ex-drinkers who quit for health reasons have a higher risk of death or disease than the general population, including moderate drinkers. This makes moderate drinkers appear healthier in comparison,' he added. While the study doesn’t conclusively advise on alcohol consumption, it underscores the importance of other health strategies. 'Australians should not rely on alcohol’s supposed health benefits as an excuse to drink, and the alcohol industry should avoid using health claims to promote products,' Assoc Prof Stamatakis concluded. 'Instead, focus on proven health strategies like regular exercise and an active lifestyle.'
translated_content: Po darbo pasigerti keli vyno stikliai gali būti daugiau žalos nei naudos, teigia naujas Universiteto Sidnėjuje tyrimas. Nors daugybė ankstesnių tyrimų rodė, kad vidutiniškas alkoholio vartojimas gali apsaugoti nuo širdies ligų, šis naujas tyrimas paneigia šią nuomonę. Tyrimas, pavadinimu 'Alkoholio Nykstantys Sveikatos Privalumai', ištirto ryšį tarp alkoholio vartojimo ir mirtingumo skirtingose amžiaus grupėse, siekdamas nustatyti tinkamus amžiaus specifinius alkoholio limitus ir geriau apibrėžti 'negeriantys'. Vienas iš tyrimo autorų, Sidnėjaus Universiteto Sveikatos Mokslų Fakulteto ir Čarlzo Perkinso Centro docentas Emmanuel Stamatakis pažymėjo, kad ankstesnieji tyrimai dažnai perdėdavo kasdienio vidutinio gėrimo privalumus. Jis paaiškino, kad šie tyrimai buvo suklaidinti, įtraukdami negeriančius be jokių priežasčių, kaip sveikatos problemos ar asmeniniai pasirinkimai. Naujajame požiūryje tyrėjai pradžioje palygino vidutinio gėrimo geriančius su buvusiais gerėjais ir rado apsaugines naudas visose amžiaus grupėse. Tačiau atskyrus niekada negėrusius kaip atskirą grupę, šios naudos išnyko. 'Ankstesni tyrimai įtraukdavo negeriančius be jokių skirtumų, kodėl jie nedrisko. Šioje grupėje gali būti tie, kurie niekada nedrisko, tie, kurie nustojo dėl sveikatos patarimų, arba tie, turintys gėrimo problemas,' teigė doc. Stamatakis. 'Buvę gerėjai, nustoję dėl sveikatos priežasčių, turi didesnį mirties ar ligos riziką nei likusi populiacijos dalis, įskaitant vidutinio gėrimo geriančius. article_content: Alex Mowatt scored the only goal as Leeds dented Middlesbrough's Sky Bet Championship title aspirations with a smash-and-grab 1-0 win. The midfielder scored in the third minute as Middlesbrough, who entered the day's early kick-off one point clear at the top of the table, suffered their first home defeat since August. Aitor Karanka's men headed into the afternoon's early game brimming with confidence having risen above Derby and Bournemouth with a 1-1 draw at Birmingham on Wednesday. Mowatt (center) watches as his third-minute shot is deflected into the goal for Leeds to beat Middlesbrough. Mowatt (center) of Leeds scored the first goal for his team after three minutes against Middlesbrough. Luke Murphy (right) of Leeds tries to protect possession from Middlesbrough striker Kike (left). Sol Bamba (right) slides across and blocks an attempt by Middlesbrough striker Kike (second right). Middlesbrough manager Aitor Karanka has taken his side to the top of the Championship table. Middlesbrough: Mejias, Nsue (Bamford, 66), Kalas, Gibson, Friend, Adomah, Clayton, Leadbitter (Forshaw, 79), Reach (Tomlin, 57), Vossen, Garcia. Subs not used: Ripley, Husband, Whitehead, Omeruo. Leeds: Silvestri, Wootton, Bamba, Bellusci (Cooper, 90), Charlie Taylor, Murphy, Cook, Byram, Austin, Mowatt, Morison. Subs not used: Sharp, Cani, Berardi, Stuart Taylor, Sloth, Antenucci. Goal: Mowatt, 3. Referee: Andre Marriner. But they got off to a terrible start when Mowatt put the visitors ahead with a deflected strike. Middlesbrough responded well but, despite creating a glut of chances in the opening period, they could not find a way past the dogged rearguard led by Leeds skipper Sol Bamba. It was the same story after half-time, welcome news for Middlesbrough's rivals Derby and Bournemouth in the promotion battle. Middlesbrough's position did not stop Karanka continuing his rotation policy, with six changes made to the side that started in midweek. It was the sole enforced alteration that proved Boro's undoing, though, as Leeds took an immediate lead. Tomas Mejias, in the XI because Dimi Konstantopoulos was serving a suspension for his red card versus the Blues, saw a poor throw-out intercepted by Lewis Cook. And the midfielder took full advantage, pulling back for Mowatt to fire into the bottom corner via a deflection. Middlesbrough almost bounced back immediately, only for Jelle Vossen to fluff his lines having been picked out by Grant Leadbitter's well-worked free-kick. The home side looked the most likely to score thereafter, with Kike and Vossen drawing smart saves from Marco Silvestri. Vossen then went agonizingly close to leveling when Giuseppe Bellusci cleared off the line to deny the Belgian after good work from Kike and Adam Reach. The onslaught showed few signs of halting as only last-ditch defending, and excellent saves from Silvestri to deny Kike and Adam Clayton, kept Leeds ahead at half-time. Leeds United have been on an upturn in form in recent matches under Neil Redfearn's guidance. Giuseppe Bellusci of Leeds (right) challenges Kike (left) during the match at the Riverside Stadium. Adam Clayton (left) of Middlesbrough tries to take the ball beyond Leeds' Steve Morison (right). Picking up where they left off, Middlesbrough applied further pressure following the interval, Kike seeing an effort turned around the post by Silvestri. But Leeds issued a warning shot of their own moments later when Scott Wootton nodded James Murphy's free-kick against the crossbar. Any thoughts that his effort may herald a spell of visiting pressure were quickly extinguished, Silvestri again called into action by Kike and Albert Adomah. Karanka introduced top-scorer Patrick Bamford midway through the second period in a bid to find an elusive equalizer. Scott Wootton of Leeds (left) challenges Middlesbrough's Adam Reach (right) for the ball. Jelle Vossen (center) lies injured and the game was halted for five minutes as he received treatment. Clayton (left) puts in a challenge on Murphy (right) of Leeds during the Championship encounter. Yet even switching to 4-2-4 did not bring the desired goal, with Bamba denying Kike after a sublime move. Frustration then turned to worry inside the Riverside as Vossen was stretchered off with what appeared to be a serious head injury. That meant there were nine minutes of injury time, although Middlesbrough - down to 10 men having used three substitutes - could not force themselves level.

article_content: Fiorentina's coach, Vincenzo Montella, has hinted that his squad may have come out ahead in the deal that saw Mohamed Salah join La Viola on loan as part of Juan Cuadrado's transfer to Chelsea. The London club shelled out £27 million to acquire Cuadrado from the Serie A side, with Salah included in the exchange. Following a strong showing from Salah and the substantial financial gain, Montella feels Fiorentina has managed the loss of their former star player quite effectively. Egyptian winger Mohamed Salah transferred to Fiorentina on loan during the January window. Chelsea spent £27 million to acquire Juan Cuadrado from Fiorentina, with Salah moving in the opposite direction as part of the deal. Salah netted Fiorentina's second goal in their 2-0 Europa League victory over Tottenham on Thursday. After Salah's goal helped secure a 2-0 win against Tottenham in the Europa League, Montella shared his thoughts with Goal.com, stating, 'Who benefited more from the Cuadrado exchange? Fiorentina made a significant profit and, performance-wise, the players are comparable.' He added, 'Salah is a player who, even if he takes occasional breaks, is lethal over short distances.' Fiorentina presently sits fifth in Serie A with 39 points, trailing third-place Napoli by six points for the final Champions League qualifying spot. They aim to close this gap starting with their upcoming match against Inter Milan on Sunday. Montella has commended Salah's contributions since his January arrival, highlighting his positive impact on the team.

article_content: By Daily Mail Reporter. UPDATED: 10:40 EST, 5 December 2011. His daughter’s serious health condition makes her life 'measured in days and weeks' - so it’s fair to question why he wants to run for president. But Republican candidate Rick Santorum, 53, says his daughter Bella’s genetic disorder Trisomy 18 is actually spurring him on in the race. The former Pennsylvania senator said he was focused on running to ensure the U.S. continues to 'respect' the lives of children like Bella. Scroll down for video. Together: Republican presidential candidate Rick Santorum, 53, says his daughter Bella's genetic disorder Trisomy 18 is spurring him on. Serious illness: He has revealed his fears about the effects of socialized medicine on children like Bella. Father and daughter: Trisomy 18 is a genetic disorder in which a person has a third copy of material from chromosome 18, instead of the usual two copies. The father-of-seven was asked to 'justify' how he could focus on the Presidential campaign trail by Christiane Amanpour on This Week. She said: 'As a mother, I just wonder how you can keep going and how you justify this with so much personal toll at home... given the polls?' He is now polling just five percent in Iowa, trailed only by Jon Huntsman, but claimed he does not worry about this. ‘I don't worry about the polls,’ Mr. Santorum said. ‘I worry about what I'm trying to do to be the best father and husband I can be. And obviously a big part of that is making sure that we have a country that respects her life and a country that is free and safe and prosperous for all of my children. Trisomy 18 is a genetic disorder in which a person has a third copy of material from chromosome 18, instead of the usual two copies. It can cause a range of problems including severe developmental delays, holes in the heart, and kidney failure. Half of infants with this condition do not survive beyond the first week of life. Some have survived to teen years - but with serious medical and developmental problems. 'And I just felt like given this is really I believe the most critical election in the history of the country that I had to step up and make sacrifices, like everybody does, to make our country a better country.' Mr. Santorum's remarks come two months after he revealed his fears about the effects of socialized medicine on children like Bella. 'Life expectancy wasn't particularly long, and just the idea of going off and doing something like this (running for president) was something I really struggled with.’ He said ‘those on the margins of life are treated differently’ in every ‘socialized-medicine country - which is absolutely where we're headed’, reported the Washington Post. 'They're not given the care, the resources aren't allocated because it is very costly, and my little girl would probably be seen as - I hear, not only from anecdotal but actual evidence from other countries - that children like this simply do not get care.' article_content: An elderly truck driver who killed a 43-year-old woman and injured her mother as they walked on a New York street will not face criminal charges. Police said James McDonald, 86, veered across East Genesee Street in Syracuse, hitting college professor Jennifer Cook and her mother, Barbara Cook, in March. Jennifer Cook died in a nearby hospital, while her 72-year-old mother suffered critical injuries but was later released. McDonald, however, has not been charged over the death. He was let off with a ticket for passing a red light and failing to keep right, Syracuse Police Sergeant Gary Bulinski told Syracuse.com. Tragic: Rhode Island College professor Jennifer Cook (pictured left and right) was killed when driver James McDonald plowed his truck into her in March. Loving family: Jennifer Cook (third from left, back row) is survived by her spouse, Moira Collins (fourth from right, back row) who is also a professor. Sgt. Bulinski said police actively investigated the crash and neither McDonald's age nor the weather seemed to be factors. He said McDonald, from Chittenango, held a valid driver's license and was not involved in recent accidents. The road was also clear. McDonald refused to comment when contacted by Syracuse.com. 'I don't care to talk about it, sorry,' he said before hanging up. The tragic incident unfolded on March 14 when Jennifer Cook and her mother were walking to a restaurant for lunch after a doctor's visit about 1:15 p.m. Cook, a Rhode Island College English professor, was in Central New York to visit her dying 93-year-old father, Frank Cook. Syracuse.com reported that McDonald plowed into the Cooks after swerving to avoid rear-ending a stationary vehicle ahead of him. The women were rushed to Upstate University Hospital where Jennifer Cook, from Rhode Island, died from her injuries. Her father Frank Cook died two weeks later. Scene: Police said James McDonald, 86, veered across the 900 block of East Genesee Street in Syracuse (pictured), near Phoebe's restaurant, hitting two pedestrians. Jennifer Cook's tragic death shocked and saddened students and staff at Rhode Island College, where she'd worked since 2004. 'Dr. Jennifer Cook was a well-liked and well-respected member of the English department and of the educational studies department,' college president Nancy Carriuolo said in a statement, according to Providence Journal. 'We all thought that Jen, who was tenured a few years ago, had a long career ahead of her at Rhode Island College.' Cook, who received degrees from American University and the University of Massachusetts, was the executive director of the Rhode Island Writing Project which worked to train young teachers. 'She was a really extraordinary teacher. She had such an amazing impact on her students,' Ronald Pitt, vice president of academic affairs at RIC, told Providence Journal. 'It was an amazing thing to see her work.' English department chair, Daniel Scott, said Cook 'inspired and trained hundreds of students who are now teachers in Rhode Island and around the country'. Cook is survived by her spouse, Moira Collins, who is also a professor.

Dženifer Kuk mirė netoliese esančioje ligoninėje, o jos 72 metų motina patyrė sunkius sužalojimus, bet vėliau buvo išleista. Makdonaldas nebuvo kaltinamas dėl mirties. Jis buvo atleistas su biletu už važiavimą per raudoną šviesoforą ir nesilaikymą dešinėje, Sirakūzų policijos seržantas Garis Bulinskis pranešė Syracuse.com. Tragičia: Rod Ailando koledžo profesorė Dženifer Kuk (pavaizduota kairėje ir dešinėje) buvo nužudyta, kai vairuotojas Džeimsas Makdonaldas kovo mėnesį įsirėžė į ją sunkvežimiu. Meili šeima: Dženifer Kuk (trečias nuo kairės, antras eilės gale) liko gyva su sutuoktine Moira Kolins (ketvirtas nuo dešinės, antras eilės gale), kuri taip pat yra profesorė. Serž. Bulinskis teigė, kad policija aktyviai tyrė avariją ir nei Makdonaldo amžius, nei oras nebuvo veiksniais. Jis teigė, kad Makdonaldas, iš Čitenango, turėjo galiojantį vairuotojo pažymėjimą ir nebuvo įsivėlęs į neseniai įvykusius avarijas. Kelias taip pat buvo laisvas. Makdonaldas atsisakė komentuoti, kai su juo susisiekė Syracuse.com. 'Aš nenoriu kalbėti apie tai, atsiprašau', jis pasakė prieš pakabinant garsiakalbį. Tragičios avarijos įvyko kovo 14 dieną, kai Dženifer Kuk ir jos motina po gydytojo vizito apie 13.15 val. einant į restoraną pietauti. Kuk, Rod Ailando koledžo anglų kalbos profesorė, buvo Centrinėje Niujorke aplankyti mirštantį 93 metų tėvą Franką Kuką. Syracuse.com pranešė, kad Makdonaldas įsirėžė į Kukus, nukrypęs nuo susidūrimo su stovinčiu priekyje automobiliu. Moterys buvo nugabentos į Upstate universiteto ligoninę, kur Dženifer Kuk iš Rod Ailando mirė nuo sužalojimų. Jos tėvas Frankas Kukas mirė po dvi savaites. Scena: Policija teigė, kad Džeimsas Makdonaldas, 86 metų, nukrypo nuo 900 East Genesee gatvės bloko Sirakūzuose (pavaizduota), netoli restorano Phoebe's, įsirėždamas į du pėsčius. Dženifer Kuk tragiška mirtis šokiravo ir nuliudo studentus ir darbuotojus Rod Ailando koledže, kur ji dirbo nuo 2004 metų. 'Dr. Dženifer Kuk buvo mėgstama ir gerbiama anglų kalbos skyriaus ir švietimo studijų skyriaus narė', koledžo prezidentė Nensi Karijuolo sakė pareiškime, remiantis Providence Journal. 'Mes visi manėme, kad Džen, kuri prieš keletą metų gavo profesūrą, dar ilgai dirbs Rod Ailando koledže.' Kuk, kuri gavo laipsnius Amerikos universitete ir Masačusetso universitete, buvo Rod Ailando rašymo projekto vykdomoji direktorė, kuris rengė jaunų mokytojų mokymą. 'Ji buvo išskirtinė mokytoja. Ji turėjo tokį nuostabų poveikį savo studentams', Rod Ailando koledžo akademinių reikalų viceprezidentas Ronaldas Pitas pasakė Providence Journal. 'Tai buvo nuostabu pamatyti jos darbą.' Anglų kalbos skyriaus pirmininkė Danielis Skotas sakė, kad Kuk 'įkvėpė ir išmokė šimtus studentų, kurie dabar mokytojai Rod Ailande ir visoje šalyje'. Kuk paliko sutuoktinę Moira Kolins, kuri taip pat yra profesorė.
